decision: Founder decision 2026-11-24 (option 2): historical divergences between the migration chain and prisma/schema.prisma are accepted TEMPORARILY, one by one, until a data-checked correction is prepared. Not a tolerance: any statement or catalogue fact not listed here fails CI, and so does a listed divergence that changes or disappears.
evidence: CI run 45451931608 (commit 438a828ea), job « Migration chain replay »: identical `prisma migrate diff` on the fresh chain-built database and on both existing-history databases; catalogue facts read on a chain-built PostgreSQL 16.
scope: public schema of a database built ONLY from prisma/migrations. Says nothing about staging or production, which were never read.

entries.statement: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "MerchantPayoutLedger_stripeTransferId_key" ON "MerchantPayoutLedger"("stripeTransferId")

fact.value: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "MerchantPayoutLedger_stripeTransferId_key" ON public."MerchantPayoutLedger" USING btree ("stripeTransferId") WHERE ("stripeTransferId" IS NOT NULL)

entries.reason: Migration 20260705150000 creates the unique index as PARTIAL (WHERE NOT NULL); Prisma cannot represent a partial index and asks for a plain one. On a chain-built database uniqueness of non-null transfer ids IS enforced. Read-only check of 2026-11-25: present on staging AND production with exactly this partial definition, valid / ready / live, 0 duplicated non-null values. Details: docs/STRIPE-TRANSFER-UNIQUE-INDEX.md.
entries.risk: HIGH on any database where the index is really absent — the same Stripe transfer could be recorded twice in the payout ledger (not the case on staging / production as of 2026-11-25)
